html:
The Nouméa Accord, signed in 1998 by France, the Kanak independence movement and the loyalists, set out a slow transfer of powers to New Caledonia and a vote on independence.

It followed the Matignon Accords of 1988, signed after the Ouvéa crisis by Jean-Marie Tjibaou. The accord recognised the wrongs of colonisation, created a local citizenship and a restricted electoral roll, and gave the provinces control of much of the nickel industry.

Three referendums were held in 2018, 2020 and 2021; each rejected independence, the last boycotted by Kanak parties. The fight over who may vote led to the riots of 2024.
sum: The Nouméa Accord, signed in 1998 by France, the Kanak independence movement and the loyalists, set out a slow transfer of powers to New Caledonia and a vote on independence.
